questions.stem: A bank teller notices that a customer made five separate cash deposits of $3,000 each over two days, apparently to avoid a reporting threshold. This activity is most characteristic of which stage of money laundering?
questions.explanation: Breaking up cash deposits into amounts below the $10,000 CTR threshold is structuring, a technique used during the placement stage to introduce illicit cash into the financial system. Layering involves moving funds among accounts to obscure their origin, which occurs after placement.

questions.stem: A broker-dealer must file a Currency Transaction Report (CTR) with FinCEN when a customer conducts cash transactions exceeding what amount in a single business day?
questions.explanation: A CTR must be filed for cash transactions exceeding $10,000 (single or aggregated same-day). The $5,000 figure is the threshold associated with SAR filings, not CTRs.

questions.stem: Under FINRA Rule 3310, every member firm's AML compliance program must, at a minimum, be tested:
choices: Only when a suspicious activity is detected
questions.explanation: FINRA Rule 3310 requires an independent test of the AML program on a periodic basis. FINRA does not directly perform the test, and testing is not contingent on detecting suspicious activity.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes "front running"?
choices: Executing a personal trade ahead of a known imminent customer block order
Buying a security at the open to drive up the closing price
Selling securities short without first locating shares to borrow
Recommending unsuitable trades to generate commissions
questions.explanation: Front running is trading for one's own account based on knowledge of a pending customer block order that will likely move the market. The other choices describe marking the open/close, naked short selling, and churning/unsuitable recommendations, respectively.

questions.stem: Under the Insider Trading and Securities Fraud Enforcement Act, the SEC may seek a civil penalty against a person who trades on material nonpublic information of up to:
choices: One time the profit gained or loss avoided
Two times the profit gained or loss avoided
Three times the profit gained or loss avoided
Five times the profit gained or loss avoided
questions.explanation: Section 21A authorizes a civil penalty of up to three times (treble) the profit gained or loss avoided as a result of the unlawful trading or communication.

questions.stem: Under FINRA Rule 5130, which of the following individuals would generally be considered a "restricted person" prohibited from purchasing a new equity issue at the public offering price?
choices: A retired schoolteacher with no industry affiliation
A registered representative employed by a FINRA member firm
An accredited investor who is a doctor
A senior corporate executive of a non-financial public company
questions.explanation: Rule 5130 defines restricted persons to include FINRA member firms and their associated persons (including registered representatives), among others. Retail customers without industry ties are not restricted simply because they are accredited or executives.

questions.stem: Under FINRA Rule 2165, after a member firm places an initial temporary hold on a disbursement based on a reasonable belief of financial exploitation of a specified adult, the hold may be extended internally for an additional period, for a total internal hold of up to:
questions.explanation: Following the 2022 amendments, Rule 2165 permits an initial 15-business-day hold plus an additional 10 business days of internal extension, for a total of 25 business days. Further extension up to 55 business days is allowed only when the matter has been reported to a state regulator, agency, or court.

questions.stem: Under FINRA Rule 4512, when opening a non-institutional account, the firm must make reasonable efforts to obtain the name and contact information of a:
questions.explanation: Rule 4512 requires firms to make reasonable efforts to obtain the name and contact information of a trusted contact person at account opening. A trusted contact is distinct from a beneficiary, POA holder, or successor owner.

questions.stem: Under TCPA cold-calling rules, an unsolicited telemarketing call to a prospective retail customer may only be made between which hours, measured in the called party's local time?
questions.explanation: Cold calls may only be made between 8 AM and 9 PM in the called party's local time zone. The caller must also identify themselves, the firm, and the firm's phone number, and screen against the firm's DNC list and the National DNC Registry.

questions.stem: Under FINRA Rule 2210, which classification applies to a written communication distributed to more than 25 retail investors within any 30-calendar-day period?
questions.explanation: A retail communication is any written communication distributed to more than 25 retail investors within a 30-day period. Correspondence is sent to 25 or fewer retail investors, and institutional communications are directed only to institutional investors.

questions.stem: A customer's brokerage account has no activity during the most recent calendar quarter. How often must the firm send the customer an account statement?
questions.explanation: Account statements must be sent at least quarterly. Statements are sent monthly when there is account activity during the month, but quarterly remains the minimum frequency regardless of activity.

questions.stem: Under Regulation S-P, a broker-dealer must provide a customer with an initial privacy notice describing the firm's information-sharing practices:
choices: Only if the customer requests it in writing
At the time the customer relationship is established
Within 30 days after the first transaction
Only when nonpublic information is shared with a third party
questions.explanation: Regulation S-P requires delivery of an initial privacy notice at the time the customer relationship is established, and an annual notice thereafter. Delivery is not contingent on a customer request or on actual third-party sharing.
